findings.where: First screen, Mark's first-person paragraph under the heading ("I advise multilateral development banks…"), at both widths and worst on the phone, where it runs to eight lines
findings.fault: Mark's opening sentence is set as a block of bold, widely spaced capitals in the sans. Long text in capitals is slow to read, and it shouts. It sits directly above a second paragraph that is set as calm serif body text, so the two paragraphs of Mark's one introduction look like two different kinds of text. It also breaks the tile's own type plan, which keeps the sans for notes and labels only.
findings.who_objects: The visitor, development-bank staff reading who Mark is: this is the one sentence that says what he does, and it is the hardest text on the screen to read. The founder would object too, because the brief asks for this tile's homepage to read like the first page of a well-set brief with a short first-person paragraph. Spaced bold capitals read as a corporate tagline, and the brief warns against that look ('a corporate tagline', 'a look any consultancy could own').

findings.where: Margin notes in the first screen (Istanbul 2025, Melbourne 2026, São Paulo 2024) and the specimen section labels (Palette, Type, Texture, Article page, Motion, Tile notes)
findings.fault: Plain text that does nothing is set in the house blue, the same blue the page uses for its buttons, the Download control, 'Replay the entrance' and the footer email link. In the first screen, the blue notes sit beside the blue 'Write to me' and 'Book a consultation' buttons, so the colour no longer tells the visitor what can be clicked.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who clicks a blue talk title such as 'LLM Course on PPP Law' expecting it to open the talk, and nothing happens. The house text-presentation rule also objects: a colour that marks links or actions never colours text that isn't a link.

findings.where: Motion sketch timing table, Start and Length columns, at both widths
findings.fault: The columns are too narrow for their values, so numbers break away from their units ('120 / ms', '900 / ms', 'on / hover'). Every row becomes two ragged lines, and a figure can't be read at a glance.
findings.who_objects: The founder and Mark, who read this table to check the timings. Each value has to be put back together across a line break.
